prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed high school in the Science and Technology modality and have knowledge of chemistry at the second-year high school level.

learning_outcomes.text: Know the main pollutants of water and the atmosphere.
Know the main water purification systems in industry.
Know the main systems for removing pollutants from a gas stream.
Design and dimension a water purification system for a specific type of industry.
Know the main solid waste disposal systems and their possible valorization.
Know the main treatments for hazardous waste in industry.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to wastewater and its pollutants - Types of wastewater - Water pollution - Characteristics of wastewater - Legal framework
Wastewater treatment plants - Urban wastewater treatment plants - Industrial wastewater treatment plants - Small treatment plants
Pre-treatment - Inlet overflow - Coarse screening - Fine screening - Grit removal - Grease removal

Physico-chemical treatment - Colloidal suspensions - Coagulation - Flocculation - Coagulation and flocculation chambers - pH modification - Heavy metal removal. Definition of heavy metal. Solubility diagrams of metals - Oxidation - Adsorption - Sedimentation

Secondary treatment I - Fundamentals of microbiology - Factors influencing biological purification - Activated sludge treatment - Nutrient removal: nitrogen and phosphorus - Functional schemes - Aeration systems
Secondary treatment II - Biological trickling filter treatment - Rotating biological contactors (biodiscs and biocylinders) - Lagooning treatment - Green filter treatment - Septic tanks
Sludge line - Thickening - Stabilization - Dewatering - Composting - Thermal reduction - Sludge application to soil

The atmosphere and pollution - Vertical structure of the atmosphere - Atmospheric pollutants - Legal framework - Types of pollutant sources - Control of atmospheric emissions - Dispersion of atmospheric pollutants - Temperature inversions - Air pollution monitoring networks - Weather stations
Particulate matter (PM) control systems - Cyclones - Gas scrubbers - Bag filters - Electrostatic precipitators
NOx and SO2 control systems - Selective non-catalytic reduction (SNCR) - Selective catalytic reduction (SCR) - Absorption - Adsorption - Use of low-sulfur fuels
The Kyoto Protocol - The Kyoto Protocol - IPCC reports - Flexibility mechanisms of the Kyoto Protocol
Urban solid waste (USW) - Waste - Legal framework of USW - Waste production - Characteristics of waste - Management phases - Transport and transfer stations - Disposal and final management
Hazardous waste - Hazardous waste identification systems - Hazardous waste management - Labeling - Storage - Technologies for hazardous waste disposal
assessment_rules: To pass the course, it is necessary to obtain a grade equal to or greater than 4 out of 10 in the total score for 'written exams', and a grade equal to or greater than 4 out of 10 in the total score for 'assignments and projects'. For the 'assignments and projects' section, submission of all proposed assignments is mandatory. To pass this section, a minimum grade of 3.0 out of 10 must be obtained in each assignment, and an average grade of at least 4.0 out of 10 must be achieved across all assignments. If any of these requirements are not met, this section will be considered failed, and the final grade for the section will be the average of the grades obtained, capped at a maximum of 4.0 points. If the critical evaluation criterion for written exams and assignments/projects is not met, the total course grade will be a FAIL, with the resulting sum of grades from all assessment systems capped at a maximum of 4.5 points. Non-recoverable activities may be replaced by similar activities with a different completion deadline or by other equivalent assessment tests for students with partial dedication to study.
